chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Wasiti, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mundhir ibn Yazid, from Yunus ibn Thibyan, who said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever fasts on a hot day and is afflicted with thirst, Allah appoints one thousand angels to wipe his face and give him glad tidings. Once he breaks his fast, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "How sweet is your fragrance and your spirit! O My angels, bear witness that I have forgiven him."

key_terms.ظمأ: Thirst - used here to emphasize the physical hardship of fasting in extreme heat
key_terms.غفرت: Forgiveness - divine pardon granted as a reward for the sacrifice of fasting
key_terms.ملك: Angel - heavenly being assigned to comfort and encourage the fasting person

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting on a hot day in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) describes the immense spiritual reward of fasting on a hot day. This teaching, narrated during the Eighty-Sixth Assembly in Rajab 368 AH, highlights that the physical suffering of thirst while fasting attracts divine attention: one thousand angels comfort the fasting person, and upon breaking the fast, God Himself declares His forgiveness. The hadith underscores the Islamic principle that sincere worship through physical hardship earns extraordinary divine mercy.
